review: 1:1–1:4 — four participles in the Arabic (accepting, following, denying, wearing); Hebrew uses a participle then finite verbs, because a chain of four participles would read as a list rather than a confession.
1:4 אֶשָּׂא חֶרְפַּת בּוּז — 'I shall bear the reproach of shame'; חֶרְפָּה is the biblical word for the shame of the cross (Ps 69:8), and בּוּז sharpens it.
2:4 לִי בַּעֲדוֹ — 'is mine for His sake', for لِي مَا دَامَ لِي ('mine while He is mine'); the Hebrew idiom is shorter and keeps the line at eight.
3:6 מִגְדַּל־עֹז — Proverbs 18:10, the fixed glossary phrase for a strong fortress; it recurs in the refrain of hymn 6.
4:2 כְּגֵר וְתוֹשָׁב — 'as a stranger and a sojourner' (Gen 23:4); the Arabic نَزِيلًا غَرِيبًا is exactly this pair.
4:5 and 4:8 both render the Arabic refrain 'peace and eternity'; the second is shortened to four syllables because the Arabic shortens it there too (وَسَلَامٌ وَخُلُود).
